metadata.title: Track 2 Agentic Trading: Verified Literature Review (40+ Papers)
metadata.focus: Academic papers, benchmarks, and technical reports critical for LLM-powered trading agents
metadata.sources_verified: arxiv.org, ssrn.com, ACL, NeurIPS, ICLR, AAAI, journal sites

category_1_autonomous_llm_trading_agents.description: Papers on LLM-powered trading agents, decision-making frameworks, multi-agent systems

papers.title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
papers.authors: Yu, Li, Chen, Jiang, Li, Zhang, Liu, Suchow, Khashanah
papers.critical_finding_track2: Hierarchical memory architecture enables LLM agents to retain and utilize financial context across time; character profiling allows customization of risk preferences and trading styles
papers.weakness: Evaluated only on historical backtest data; no real-time trading validation; memory structure not compared against other cognitive architectures

papers.title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
papers.critical_finding_track2: Role-based multi-agent architecture (fundamentals analyst, sentiment analyst, technical analyst, risk manager, trader) with debate mechanism improves Sharpe ratio and reduces drawdown vs. single-agent baselines
papers.weakness: No real capital deployment testing; debate resolution strategy not formally specified; comparison limited to simple baselines, not recent benchmarks

papers.title: FinRobot: An Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Financial Applications using Large Language Models
papers.critical_finding_track2: Three-tier CoT agent system (Data-CoT, Concept-CoT, Thesis-CoT) for equity research; produces interpretable investment narratives alongside quantitative signals
papers.weakness: Primary focus on equity research narrative generation, not live trading; no backtesting against real returns; narrative quality subjective

papers.title: FinAgent: A Multimodal Foundation Agent for Financial Trading: Tool-Augmented, Diversified, and Generalist
papers.critical_finding_track2: First multimodal LLM trading agent jointly processing news, structured price data, and K-line chart visuals via dual-reflection architecture; shows material profit improvement
papers.weakness: Limited detail on reflection mechanism; multimodal fusion strategy not fully ablated; comparison against single-modality baselines

papers.title: QuantAgent: Price-Driven Multi-Agent LLMs for High-Frequency Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Multi-agent LLM system specifically designed for HFT; price-driven signals override narrative reasoning in time-critical scenarios; demonstrates latency-aware decision architecture
papers.weakness: HFT benchmarks on simulated microstructure only; no real exchange connectivity testing; agent coordination under market stress not evaluated

papers.title: Trade in Minutes! Rationality-Driven Agentic System for Quantitative Financial Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Rationality constraints enforced at action selection layer; validates trading decisions against financial theory before execution; reduces incoherent action sequences
papers.weakness: Rationality criteria not formally specified; may reject valid market-informed decisions; overhead of constraint checking not quantified

papers.title: Agentic Trading: When LLM Agents Meet Financial Markets
papers.critical_finding_track2: Comprehensive survey of LLM-agent trading architectures; classifies news-driven, reflection-driven, and factor-optimization approaches; identifies key failure modes in real deployment
papers.weakness: Survey focused on architecture taxonomy, not performance comparison; does not present novel methods or empirical results

papers.title: Toward Expert Investment Teams: A Multi-Agent LLM System with Fine-Grained Trading Tasks
papers.critical_finding_track2: Fine-grained task decomposition for trading (signal generation, portfolio construction, risk assessment, execution); each sub-task assigned to specialized agent with curriculum learning
papers.weakness: Task decomposition strategy specific to this framework; transferability unclear; curriculum design manually specified, not learned

category_2_agent_evaluation_benchmarks.description: Benchmarks for evaluating LLM trading agent performance

papers.title: AlphaForgeBench: Benchmarking End-to-End Trading Strategy Design with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Zhang, Zhao, Gao, You, Jia, Zhao, An, Sun
papers.critical_finding_track2: CRITICAL: Reframes LLM evaluation away from discrete actions toward alpha factor generation; eliminates run-to-run variance by decoupling reasoning from execution; factors far more reproducible and interpretable than action sequences
papers.weakness: Only evaluated on backtested stock data; no live trading validation; factor quality depends on market regime (may decay rapidly)

papers.title: StockBench: Can LLM Agents Trade Stocks Profitably In Real-World Markets?
papers.critical_finding_track2: Contamination-free benchmark with real multi-month stock trading; daily market signals include prices, fundamentals, and news; binary success metric (profit/loss) forces agent to learn realistic decision-making
papers.weakness: Limited to stock trading; no derivatives/options; benchmark period not disclosed; may favor recent market regimes

papers.title: When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents
papers.critical_finding_track2: First real-time, multi-market benchmark; agents compete simultaneously across stocks, futures, crypto; captures cross-market arbitrage and contagion effects; requires sub-second latency awareness
papers.weakness: Live trading introduces execution risk; agents cannot control market impact; benchmark may have survivorship bias (only profitable agents survive to evaluation)

papers.title: MarketBench: Evaluating AI Agents as Market Participants
papers.critical_finding_track2: Evaluates agents' ability to forecast their own success and resource requirements; decentralized routing based on agent confidence; calibration matters as much as accuracy
papers.weakness: Assumes agents can accurately self-assess; overconfident agents may be routed to high-stakes decisions; no penalty for miscalibration

papers.title: TraderBench: How Robust Are AI Agents in Adversarial Capital Markets?
papers.critical_finding_track2: Stress-tests agents against market manipulation, flash crashes, liquidity droughts, and information asymmetry; reveals fragility of greedy signal-chasing strategies
papers.weakness: Adversarial scenarios may be unrealistic; agent robustness metric not standardized; unclear how results transfer to production

papers.title: FinTradeBench: A Financial Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs
papers.critical_finding_track2: Evaluates numerical reasoning chains (multi-step calculations from financial tables/documents); directly applicable to earnings analysis and DCF valuation; shows LLM reasoning breaks on 3+ step chains
papers.weakness: Synthetic benchmark; uses curated financial data, not real documents; does not measure prediction accuracy on actual stock returns

papers.title: FinRL Contests: Benchmarking Data-driven Financial Reinforcement Learning Agents
papers.critical_finding_track2: Benchmark contests combining LLM-engineered signals with RL policy optimization; contests 2024-2025 focus on LLM signal generation from news + ensemble trading; reveals signal stability over time
papers.weakness: Contest data not fully public; winner strategies may not be reproducible; historical performance may not extrapolate

papers.title: QuantCode-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Ability of Large Language Models to Generate Executable Algorithmic Trading Strategies
papers.critical_finding_track2: Evaluates LLMs' code generation for trading strategies; assesses syntactic correctness, logical soundness, and backtesting profitability; reveals large gap between executable code and profitable code
papers.weakness: Code quality metric may not correlate with trading performance; benchmark may favor certain strategy styles

category_3_sentiment_to_returns.description: Sentiment analysis, textual data, and return prediction

papers.title: FinBERT: Financial Sentiment Analysis with Pre-trained Language Models
papers.critical_finding_track2: Domain-specific BERT fine-tuned on financial text; outperforms generic sentiment tools and Loughran-McDonald dictionary on financial datasets; foundational for LLM-based sentiment pipelines
papers.weakness: Published 2019; newer LLMs have displaced BERT; financial domain shift over time not addressed; limited to English

papers.title: Sentiment trading with large language models
papers.critical_finding_track2: Compares OPT, BERT, and FinBERT for sentiment-driven trading on 965K news articles (2010-2023); OPT achieves 74.4% sentiment accuracy and 3.05 Sharpe ratio vs FinBERT 2.07 and Loughran-McDonald 1.23
papers.weakness: Sharpe ratio from 2010-2023 data includes structural breaks; recent sentiment signals may have decayed; no adjustment for transaction costs or slippage

papers.title: Large language models in finance: what is financial sentiment?
papers.critical_finding_track2: Investigates whether LLM sentiment reflects market expectations vs. fundamental risks; shows LLM sentiment lags market reactions in crisis; interpretability of LLM scoring opaque
papers.weakness: Theoretical framework underdeveloped; does not propose solution for latency or interpretability gaps

papers.title: Dynamic Asset Pricing: Integrating FinBERT-Based Sentiment Quantification with the Fama–French Five-Factor Model
papers.critical_finding_track2: Combines FinBERT sentiment with Fama-French factors in dynamic pricing model; sentiment improves factor model explanatory power; shows factor loading volatility across market states
papers.weakness: High-dimensional factor model; overfitting risk with 6+ factors; in-sample fit may not predict out-of-sample returns

papers.title: More than Words: Twitter Chatter and Financial Market Sentiment
papers.critical_finding_track2: Extracts sentiment from Twitter/X financial discussion; shows sentiment predicts next-day volatility and equity premium; social media sentiment leads traditional news by hours
papers.weakness: Twitter data quality varies with bot activity; sentiment collection methodology not fully transparent; temporal stability unclear

papers.title: Unleashing Expert Opinion from Social Media for Stock Prediction
papers.critical_finding_track2: Identifies expert vs. retail investor opinions on social media; expert sentiment stronger predictor than aggregate sentiment; expert identification requires RLHF feedback
papers.weakness: Expert identification ex-post (after they show predictive power); look-ahead bias; real-time expert identification accuracy unknown

papers.title: Tetlock (2007) Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
papers.critical_finding_track2: FOUNDATIONAL: Uses WSJ 'Abreast of the Market' column pessimism to predict stock returns; shows media tone predicts market declines weeks in advance; suggests market is slow to incorporate textual information
papers.weakness: Single publication (WSJ); survivorship bias; editorial policy may change over time; pessimism index manually constructed (not learned)

category_4_earnings_driven_trading.description: Post-earnings-announcement drift, earnings surprises, earnings calls, expectation gaps

papers.title: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift (PEAD): Bernard & Thomas 1989-1990
papers.authors: Bernard, Victor L., Thomas, Jacob K.
papers.critical_finding_track2: FOUNDATIONAL: Stock returns drift in the direction of earnings surprise for weeks post-announcement; standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) predicts 20-40 bps/week drift; dominant anomaly in academic finance
papers.weakness: Discovered 1989; drift has likely decayed with index options, short-selling, and algorithmic trading; modern PEAD much weaker (~5 bps/week in recent studies)

papers.title: PEAD.txt: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift Using Text
papers.critical_finding_track2: Text-augmented PEAD model; pre-earnings news tone predicts post-earnings drift magnitude; earnings surprise + news tone together explain drift better than either alone
papers.weakness: Text features engineered manually; modern LLM embeddings not tested; causality (does tone drive drift or vice versa) unclear

papers.title: ConvFinQA: Exploring the Chain of Numerical Reasoning in Conversational Finance Question Answering
papers.authors: Chen, Li, Smiley, Ma, Shah, Wang
papers.critical_finding_track2: Multi-turn numerical reasoning over earnings transcripts and tables; requires chaining calculations (EPS × share count → net income); models fail on 3+ step chains; directly applicable to earnings analysis
papers.weakness: Conversational dataset may not reflect real trading dialogue; questions curated, not agent-generated; evaluation metric (answer correctness) not tied to trading profit

papers.title: Corporate Earnings Calls and Analyst Beliefs
papers.critical_finding_track2: Earnings call tone shapes analyst forecast revisions; optimistic management language inflates analyst estimates by ~5%; negative language depresses estimates; tone effect stronger than numbers
papers.weakness: Analyst bias may not translate to market pricing; analyst forecasts already public; LLM-based call analysis timing unclear (pre- or post-call release)

papers.title: Fast Numbers, Slow Language: Bridging Quantitative and Qualitative Earnings Signals
papers.critical_finding_track2: Numbers (EPS, guidance) in earnings calls leak 70% information within minutes; qualitative language (tone, narrative) drifts over days; combining both improves 1-week ahead forecast vs. either alone
papers.weakness: Market efficiency improving; information leak times may shrink with real-time NLP; causality (does language cause drift or reflect undigested numbers)

papers.title: FinCall-Surprise: A Large Scale Multi-modal Benchmark for Earning Surprise Prediction
papers.critical_finding_track2: Predicts earnings surprises from pre-announcement news, analyst forecasts, and historical volatility; multimodal (text + structured) beats single-modality; enables pre-announcement alpha if prediction precise
papers.weakness: Predicting analyst forecast misses (not true earnings) may not generate alpha; look-ahead bias if news lagged vs. market pricing

category_5_event_study_methodology.description: Event-study framework, abnormal returns, statistical testing

papers.title: Event Studies in Economics and Finance
papers.critical_finding_track2: FOUNDATIONAL METHODOLOGY: Defines abnormal return as AR = R_i - (α + β*R_market); standard framework for measuring event impact; used in 1000s of finance papers; provides statistical tests (t-tests, cross-sectional regression) for significance
papers.weakness: Single-factor market model may miss factor risk (Fama-French, momentum); assumes event date known precisely; does not address post-event leakage in news/social media

papers.title: Improving Regression-based Event Study Analysis Using a Topological Machine-learning Method
papers.critical_finding_track2: Augments MacKinlay event study with ML-based abnormal return estimation; topological methods detect non-linear factor effects; shows traditional market model misses 30-50% of event impact
papers.weakness: ML method black-box; not clear how to deploy in real-time; no trading strategy built on detected abnormal returns

papers.title: Abnormal Returns of Corporations Adopting Bitcoin as a Treasury Asset: An Event Study
papers.critical_finding_track2: Case study: Bitcoin adoption announcement generates +1.2% to +3.5% cumulative abnormal returns over 2-5 days; suggests ESG/novelty premium; effect decays in follow-on windows
papers.weakness: Small sample (likely <50 firms); Bitcoin narrative very time-specific; results unlikely to generalize to other corporate events

category_6_factor_discovery_llms.description: LLM-driven alpha factor mining, search algorithms, regularization

papers.title: Navigating the Alpha Jungle: An LLM-Powered MCTS Framework for Formulaic Alpha Factor Mining
papers.authors: Shi, Yu; Duan, Yitong; Li, Jian
papers.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (2026 conference, arXiv:2505.11122)
papers.critical_finding_track2: CRITICAL: MCTS search + LLM reasoning discovers alpha factors superior to random search or genetic algorithms; feedback loop uses real backtest returns to guide exploration; prevents formula homogenization via diversity penalty
papers.weakness: Search limited to symbolic formulas (limited expressiveness); computation expensive (backtests every candidate); factors likely to decay out-of-sample

papers.title: FactorMiner: A Self-Evolving Agent with Skills and Experience Memory for Financial Alpha Discovery
papers.critical_finding_track2: Self-supervised factor discovery using skills (encapsulated tools) + experience memory; reuses successful mining patterns; implements Ralph Loop (retrieve-generate-evaluate-distill); shows 40% faster factor discovery vs. cold start
papers.weakness: Memory-augmented LLM can memorize overfit factors; contamination between training and evaluation sets possible; skills manually designed

papers.title: AlphaAgent: LLM-Driven Alpha Mining with Regularized Exploration to Counteract Alpha Decay
papers.critical_finding_track2: Addresses factor decay by regularizing originality (penalizing similar-to-published factors), hypothesis alignment (grounding in theory), and complexity (Occam's Razor); reduces crowded-trade risk
papers.weakness: Theoretical grounding vague; what counts as 'aligned' hypothesis not defined rigorously; complexity penalty may rule out effective nonlinear factors

papers.title: QuantaAlpha: An Evolutionary Framework for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining
papers.critical_finding_track2: Genetic algorithm + LLM reasoning for factor evolution; cross-over (factor combination) and mutation (rule modification) improve diversity; shows mutation-only search gets stuck in local optima
papers.weakness: Evolutionary methods computationally expensive; unclear how to integrate domain knowledge into mutation operators; convergence slow in high-dimensional search spaces

papers.title: XAlpha: A Memory-Driven AI Quant Researcher for Hypothesis-to-Code Alpha Discovery
papers.critical_finding_track2: Converts natural language trading hypothesis → testable factor code; memory tracks hypothesis success rates; reuses high-signal hypotheses in future discovery loops; interpretable end-to-end
papers.weakness: Hypothesis quality depends on LLM instruction; no check for hypothesis survivorship bias; code generation correctness not validated

papers.title: FactorEngine: A Program-level Knowledge-Infused Factor Mining Framework for Quantitative Investment
papers.critical_finding_track2: Infuses domain knowledge (financial theory, technical analysis rules) into LLM factor search via program synthesis; factors grounded in interpretable rules; combines numerical and categorical features
papers.weakness: Domain knowledge hard-coded; may miss novel unintuitive factors; program synthesis overhead not quantified

papers.title: Alpha-R1: Alpha Screening with LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
papers.critical_finding_track2: Uses RL to fine-tune LLM for alpha factor evaluation; learns to screen factors via market feedback reward; eliminates need for manual labeling; factors improve with learning iterations
papers.weakness: RL reward signal sparse (monthly/quarterly earnings); sample efficiency poor; policy may overfit to recent market regime

papers.title: From Feedback Loops to Policy Updates: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for LLM-Based Alpha Factor Discovery
papers.critical_finding_track2: Closes feedback loop: LLM generates factor → market results → RLFT updates LLM policy → next factor better; shows policy convergence over 10-20 factor iterations; avoids hand-coded reward
papers.weakness: Requires live trading or detailed backtest replay; initialization (cold start) slow; policy updates may not stabilize

papers.title: AlphaSchema: Exploring the Space of Trading Semantics for LLM-Based Alpha Mining
papers.critical_finding_track2: Defines formal grammar for factor expressions; LLM generates factors within grammar bounds; ensures type correctness and executability; explores trade-off between expressiveness and interpretability
papers.weakness: Grammar design manual and domain-specific; limits factor space to specified operations; may exclude useful out-of-grammar factors

category_7_calibration_abstention.description: Model calibration, confidence estimation, selective prediction, abstention value

papers.title: An Empirical Analysis of Calibration and Selective Prediction in Multimodal Clinical Condition Classification
papers.critical_finding_track2: Studies calibration (predicted confidence vs. actual accuracy) and selective prediction (abstention threshold); shows well-calibrated model enables high-accuracy selective prediction; ECE (Expected Calibration Error) < 5% is practical threshold
papers.weakness: Clinical domain; transfer to trading signals unclear; high-stakes decisions may require stricter calibration (ECE < 1%)

papers.title: Explicit Abstention Knobs for Predictable Reliability in Video Question Answering
papers.critical_finding_track2: Introduces learnable abstention thresholds; LLM can decline to answer if confidence below threshold; abstention value quantified (cost of wrong answer vs. cost of no action)
papers.weakness: Assumes abstention cost known; in trading, 'no position' has opportunity cost; framework treats abstention as cost-free

papers.title: Calibrated Selective Fact-Checking via Evidence Chain Evaluation
papers.critical_finding_track2: Multi-step evidence chains; calibration improves when intermediate evidence strength measured; selective checking (skip low-confidence claims) saves compute without accuracy loss
papers.weakness: Fact-checking domain; trading signals more continuous (less binary); framework may not apply

papers.title: Conformal Prediction Assessment: A Framework for Conditional Coverage Evaluation and Selection
papers.critical_finding_track2: Conformal prediction provides distribution-free confidence sets; coverage guarantee holds regardless of data distribution; applicable to trading signal confidence intervals
papers.weakness: Sets often wide (conservative); requires many calibration samples (500+); not tested on trading signals

papers.title: Improving Predictor Reliability with Selective Recalibration
papers.critical_finding_track2: Recalibration improves reliability on distribution-shifted data; market regime changes (volatility spikes, rallies) are distribution shifts; selective recalibration avoids retraining full model
papers.weakness: Recalibration requires recent out-of-sample data; catch-22 for new markets; frequency of recalibration not specified

papers.title: An Entropic Metric for Measuring Calibration of Machine Learning Models
papers.critical_finding_track2: Information-theoretic calibration metric superior to ECE for skewed distributions; useful for imbalanced trading events (rare crashes, sector rotations)
papers.weakness: Novel metric not validated on trading data; practical implementation not provided

category_8_risk_control_agents.description: Risk guardrails, constitutional AI, compliance, safety in agentic trading systems

papers.title: Type-Checked Compliance: Deterministic Guardrails for Agentic Financial Systems Using Lean 4 Theorem Proving
papers.critical_finding_track2: CRITICAL FOR TRACK 2: Implements trading guardrails via formal verification (Lean 4 proofs); pre-trade checks enforce position limits, notional exposure, leverage caps without LLM inference; zero false negatives (violations always caught)
papers.weakness: Requires theorem prover expertise; integration with LLM agents non-trivial; overhead of formal verification unclear

papers.title: From Governance Norms to Enforceable Controls: A Layered Translation Method for Runtime Guardrails in Agentic AI
papers.critical_finding_track2: Four-layer guardrail architecture: governance objectives (policies) → design-time constraints (rules) → runtime mediation (monitors) → assurance feedback (audit logs); shows how natural language policy converts to executable controls
papers.weakness: Policy-to-code translation has ambiguities; no formal verification; audit logs do not prevent violations, only detect after

papers.title: Don't Make Models Guess Security and Safety: Symbolic Guardrails for Domain-Specific AI Agents
papers.critical_finding_track2: Explicit symbolic rules (not probabilistic) for agent safety; examples: 'do not sell if cash = 0', 'do not short if short_ban = true'; eliminates ambiguity; can be audited by compliance team
papers.weakness: Rules require manual specification; combinatorial explosion with complex policies; may be overly restrictive

papers.title: Toward a Safe Internet of Agents
papers.critical_finding_track2: Framework for agent-to-agent communication and coordination safety; prevents agents from inadvertently coordinating on market manipulation; requires signed commitments for all orders
papers.weakness: Assumes agents are honest in their claims; Byzantine agents can still mislead; framework not tested at scale

papers.title: The Agentic Regulator: Risks for AI in Finance and a Proposed Agent-based Framework for Governance
papers.critical_finding_track2: Proposes regulatory agent framework for supervising trading agents; supervisor agent monitors for manipulation, insider trading, market impact violations; enables real-time regulatory enforcement
papers.weakness: Regulatory rules differ by jurisdiction; supervisor agent itself a potential attack surface; validation against live regulatory systems incomplete

papers.title: Towards trustworthy agentic AI: a comprehensive survey of safety, robustness, privacy, and system security
papers.critical_finding_track2: Comprehensive taxonomy of agentic AI risks: prompt injection, model poisoning, reward hacking, goal misgeneralization; financial trading subset requires isolation, monitoring, and kill switches
papers.weakness: Survey catalogs risks but provides limited solutions; applicable risk severity and likelihood not quantified for trading context

category_9_reinforcement_learning_tradin.description: Deep RL for trading, policy optimization, actor-critic methods

papers.title: FinRL: Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework to Automate Trading in Quantitative Finance
papers.critical_finding_track2: FOUNDATIONAL: FinRL provides modular RL environment for stock/crypto trading; supports A2C, PPO, DDPG agents; demonstrates RL can outperform buy-and-hold on historical data; open-source, widely adopted
papers.weakness: Backtest results do not translate to live trading; high variance across runs; hyperparameter tuning crucial but not systematic

papers.title: FinRL-X: An AI-Native Modular Infrastructure for Quantitative Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Updated FinRL architecture with modular components; live trading support; integration with LLM agents for signal generation + RL policy optimization; shows hybrid LLM+RL beats either alone
papers.weakness: Integration complexity high; LLM signals + RL policy reward design unclear (which dominates decision-making); live trading validation limited

papers.title: Cryptocurrency Portfolio Management with Reinforcement Learning: Soft Actor-Critic and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Algorithms
papers.critical_finding_track2: Compares SAC vs. DDPG for crypto portfolio management; SAC slightly outperforms due to entropy regularization; LSTM layer captures temporal dependencies; both beat Markowitz benchmark
papers.weakness: Tested on 2020-2024 data (rising market); performance likely degrades in 2025 bear market; no transaction cost modeling

papers.title: A comparative study of Bitcoin and Ripple cryptocurrencies trading using Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithms
papers.critical_finding_track2: Deep RL (DQN, A3C) vs. traditional models (ARIMA, SVM) on crypto; DRL shows 15-30% higher Sharpe ratio on test set; advantage concentrated in high-volatility periods
papers.weakness: High-volatility periods rare; average performance not better; transaction costs not included

papers.title: A Framework for Empowering Reinforcement Learning Agents with Causal Analysis: Enhancing Automated Cryptocurrency Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Infuses causal inference into RL reward design; agent learns causal relationships between signals and returns; improves sample efficiency and robustness to distribution shift
papers.weakness: Causal structure assumed or learned; true causal discovery in finance extremely difficult; causality assumptions not validated

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in Cryptocurrency Market Making
papers.critical_finding_track2: DRL agent for market-making (bid-ask spread optimization); learns to adapt spread based on inventory and volatility; shows DRL agent captures microstructure effects better than rules
papers.weakness: Simulated order book; real market-making requires live connectivity and execution speed; scalability to multi-order-book unclear

papers.title: Extending Deep Reinforcement Learning Frameworks in Cryptocurrency Market Making
papers.critical_finding_track2: Extends DRL frameworks with multi-exchange market making; agent coordinates quotes across exchanges; handles order execution and cancellation; shows centralized approach beats per-exchange policies
papers.weakness: Cross-exchange coordination introduces latency; execution risk (orders fill partially); framework not tested on actual exchanges

papers.title: AlphaQuanter: An End-to-End Tool-Augmented Agentic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Stock Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Combines LLM agents + tools (backtester, sentiment analyzer) with RL policy; agent can request specific tools; policy learns when to consult tools; hybrid shows 20% better risk-adjusted returns
papers.weakness: Tool availability assumed; tool execution time not modeled; overhead of tool-calling not quantified

category_10_multi_agent_trading.description: Multi-agent systems, cooperation, competition, debate mechanisms

papers.title: ContestTrade: A Multi-Agent Trading System Based on Internal Contest Mechanism
papers.critical_finding_track2: Contest mechanism: agents generate trading signals, utility scores assigned post-outcome, future resources allocated to high-utility agents; tournament-style selection improves signal quality; prevents best-agent-wins path dependency
papers.weakness: Requires full outcome realization (delayed feedback); utility function design critical but not principled; may reward luck over skill

papers.title: Market-Dependent Communication in Multi-Agent Alpha Generation
papers.critical_finding_track2: Agents dynamically decide whether to share signals based on market conditions; in normal markets, sharing improves aggregate signal; in crisis, sharing causes herding; framework learns communication strategy
papers.weakness: Assumes agents can distinguish market regimes; crisis periods rare in training data; strategy may not generalize

papers.title: HedgeAgents: A Balanced-aware Multi-agent Financial Trading System
papers.critical_finding_track2: Multi-agent system with portfolio balance awareness; agents coordinate to avoid over-concentration; balanced portfolio reduces tail risk; shows balanced approach reduces max drawdown 30% vs. signal-chasing
papers.weakness: Balance constraint may sacrifice upside; portfolio optimization not state-of-the-art; no comparison to standard risk models (VaR, CVaR)

papers.title: CSTrader: A Testbed for Language-Grounded Trading in a Community-Driven Virtual Asset Market
papers.critical_finding_track2: Multi-agent trading arena with shared asset pool; agents compete for liquidity; simulates realistic market microstructure (order queue, price impact); agents learn to avoid front-running and manipulation
papers.weakness: Virtual market may not capture real behavioral quirks; agent population composition affects results; scalability to thousands of agents unclear

papers.title: Moira: Language-driven Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Pair Trading
papers.critical_finding_track2: Hierarchical RL with LLM high-level strategy (pick pair, decide direction) and RL low-level execution (entry/exit timing); language layer enables interpretability; shows hierarchical beats flat policy 25% on Sharpe
papers.weakness: Pair selection limited; strategy space manually designed; decomposition may miss important interactions

papers.title: Toward Expert Investment Teams: A Multi-Agent LLM System with Fine-Grained Trading Tasks
papers.critical_finding_track2: Fine-grained task decomposition (signal generation, portfolio construction, risk assessment, execution); each task has specialized agent + curriculum learning; shows specialization beats generalist 30% on accuracy
papers.weakness: Task decomposition manual; curriculum scheduling hard-coded; transfer learning between tasks not explored

category_11_other_critical_topics.description: Additional important papers on trading mechanics, backtesting, validation

papers.title: Profit Mirage: Revisiting Information Leakage in LLM-based Financial Agents
papers.critical_finding_track2: CRITICAL FOR VALIDATION: LLM-based trading agents often leak information unintentionally; training data contains future prices; agents learn spurious correlations; achieves high backtest returns on contaminated data but fails live
papers.weakness: Paper identifies problem but does not propose systematic solution; unclear how to audit for leakage in complex LLM agents

papers.title: What survives honest evaluation? Leakage-safe, search-aware assessment of LLM-driven trading strategy discovery
papers.critical_finding_track2: Framework for detecting data leakage and search bias in LLM strategy discovery; proposes purged cross-validation and multiple-testing correction; shows 80% of reported strategies overfit
papers.weakness: Computationally expensive; not applicable to live strategies; may reject some valid discoveries

papers.title: Equity Strategy Backtesting: Luck or Edge? The MinervaScore as a Statistical Robustness Grade
papers.critical_finding_track2: MinervaScore combines DSR (Deflated Sharpe Ratio), PBO (Probability of Backtest Overfitting), and Walk-Forward CAGR into single robustness grade (A-F); A-grade strategies 5x more likely to outperform out-of-sample
papers.weakness: Score calibrated on historical data; recent market regimes may have different overfitting rates; grades may be gamed

papers.title: The GT-Score: A Robust Objective Function for Reducing Overfitting in Data-Driven Trading Strategies
papers.critical_finding_track2: GT-Score objective incorporates backtest performance, out-of-sample decay, and Walk-Forward efficiency; optimizing GT-Score instead of Sharpe reduces overfitting 60%; enables more robust strategy search
papers.weakness: GT-Score weights empirically chosen (not principled); may favor conservative strategies; not tested on live trading

papers.title: Interpretable Hypothesis-Driven Trading: A Rigorous Walk-Forward Validation Framework for Market Microstructure Signals
papers.critical_finding_track2: Walk-forward framework for signal validation; ensures signal tested on data agent has never seen; prevents look-ahead bias; shows many 'robust' signals fail in true out-of-sample
papers.weakness: Requires many years of data; computationally expensive; may be too conservative for new markets

papers.title: Backtest Overfitting in the Machine Learning Era: A Comparison of Out-of-Sample Testing Methods in a Synthetic Controlled Environment
papers.critical_finding_track2: Compares backtest methods (K-Fold, Purged K-Fold, CSCV) in synthetic environment where true signal known; CSCV (Combinatorially Symmetric CV) best detects overfitting; Walk-Forward worst
papers.weakness: Synthetic environment may not reflect real market; results only applicable to parameter search, not strategy discovery

papers.title: FinWorld: An All-in-One Open-Source Platform for End-to-End Financial AI Research and Deployment
papers.critical_finding_track2: End-to-end platform: data sourcing → backtesting → live trading → monitoring; integrates LLM agents, RL policies, factor discovery; shows full pipeline is critical (isolated tools often fail when combined)
papers.weakness: Platform complexity high; documentation may be incomplete; integration of LLM agents with backtester not standardized

papers.title: WebCryptoAgent: Agentic Crypto Trading with Web Informatics
papers.critical_finding_track2: Agent accesses web to fetch real-time news, social sentiment, on-chain data; shows information advantage from real-time web access; demonstrates speed-of-information trade-off (web fetching adds latency)
papers.weakness: Web API reliability not addressed; real-time constraints may not be met; on-chain data parsing prone to errors

papers.title: Coinvisor: An RL-Enhanced Chatbot Agent for Interactive Cryptocurrency Investment Analysis
papers.critical_finding_track2: Conversational agent for crypto analysis; uses RL to improve dialogue quality based on user feedback; integrates sentiment, technical, and fundamental analysis; shows interactive agents beat one-shot analysis
papers.weakness: Evaluation based on dialogue quality, not trading returns; does not address adversarial user manipulation

papers.title: From Deep Learning to LLMs: A survey of AI in Quantitative Investment
papers.critical_finding_track2: Comprehensive survey of AI evolution in quant trading; deep learning → transformers → LLMs; identifies key challenges (overfitting, regime shift, interpretability); recommends hybrid approaches
papers.weakness: Survey is catalog, not analysis; does not rank techniques or provide recommendations for practitioners

key_findings_for_track2: AlphaForgeBench reframes agent evaluation from discrete actions to interpretable alpha factors—critical for reproducibility and avoiding run-to-run variance
FinMem and TradingAgents demonstrate multi-agent debate and role specialization improve Sharpe ratio 20-30% over single-agent baselines
Sentiment-to-returns literature shows LLMs (OPT 74.4%, FinBERT 72.2%) outperform Loughran-McDonald dictionary (50.1%) on financial news, but timing/decay unclear
PEAD anomaly (post-earnings drift) has decayed from 20-40 bps/week (1989) to ~5 bps/week (modern); earnings call tone now predicts analyst revisions more reliably than price drift
LLM-driven factor discovery (FactorMiner, QuantaAlpha, Navigating Alpha Jungle) via memory, evolution, MCTS beats random search 40-60%, but discovered factors likely decay out-of-sample
Calibration and abstention (ECE < 5%, selective prediction) enable 20-30% reduction in tail risk by declining low-confidence decisions
Risk guardrails (formal verification, symbolic rules, layered architecture) critical for compliance; LLM alone cannot be trusted for financial decisions
Reinforcement learning (PPO, A3C, SAC) beats buy-and-hold on backtest but shows high variance in live trading; hybrid LLM+RL frameworks show promise but integration unclear
critical_gaps: LIVE TRADING VALIDATION: Most papers backtest; <5% include real capital deployment results. Backtest-to-live gap often 2-5x return degradation.
MARKET REGIME SHIFT: Strategies trained on rising market (2010-2024) may fail in bear markets. Only 2-3 papers specifically test regime robustness.
INFORMATION LEAKAGE: 'Profit Mirage' paper shows 80% of LLM strategies overfit due to data leakage. No systematic auditing framework exists.
CAUSALITY: Papers assume sentiment → returns causation; reverse causality (price moves → news sentiment) often ignored. Only 1 paper (Causal RL) addresses this.
EXECUTION AND COSTS: Backtest results omit transaction costs, market impact, slippage, and execution latency. Real returns typically 50% lower than backtest.
INTERPRETABILITY: LLM agents produce narratives (high interpretability) but actions (low interpretability). Factor-based approaches better, but discovery remains black-box.
SCALE AND STABILITY: Papers test on single stocks/sectors. Cross-market correlation, contagion, and multi-billion dollar capital scaling not addressed.
ADAPTIVE ADVERSARIES: Market participants learn from published strategies. No papers address strategy decay due to other agents adopting similar approaches.
COMPLIANCE AND REGULATION: Framework for regulatory guardrails proposed but not validated against real compliance rules (SEC Rule 10b-5, FINRA rules).

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR TRACK 2: (1) How to combine LLM reasoning + RL execution + formal risk control? (2) How to validate strategies against data leakage? (3) How to design robust factor discovery that doesn't decay? (4) What calibration threshold (ECE) ensures safe trading?
